description: Single source of the Phase 9 rasterizer perf-regression baselines. scripts/check-raster-perf-baseline.sh diffs a measured BenchmarkDotNet run (its full JSON export) against this file's per-benchmark 'baselineMs', gated by 'toleranceFraction' (or a benchmark's own override): measured <= baselineMs * (1 + toleranceFraction) passes; a measured time over that band fails unless justified. Independently of any live measurement, the script also runs the SSIM-LOOSEN-shaped governance check: a diff that raises any baselineMs/toleranceFraction value (loosening the gate) must carry a 'PERF-LOOSEN:' commit-message token, mirroring scripts/check-ssim-threshold.sh exactly; tightening (lowering a value) always passes freely.
runner: same-platform-only (mirroring the SSIM gate's own same-platform-only constraint): the numbers below are now measured on the CI runner platform (linux-x64, GitHub Actions ubuntu-latest), replacing the original conservative mac-arm64 (Apple Silicon dev machine) Stopwatch means that were uniformly faster than CI and, for the parallel suite especially, unrepresentative of a shared 2-vCPU runner's throughput. Tolerance is deliberately generous (limits ≈ 2x the observed mean) because these are single-run observations on a shared runner with high run-to-run variance; tighten only after a multi-run statistical BenchmarkDotNet calibration on the same platform.
calibrationNote: Re-baselined against the first post-merge linux-CI run of the raster-perf-gate job (single measured run per benchmark, JSON-exported by ci.yml): text 62.85 ms, image 17.88 ms, transparency 16.87 ms, parallel 203.07 ms. The original mac-arm64 dev-machine numbers (48/9/11/53 ms) were faster than the CI runner, so the gate failed on the parallel suite (203 ms > 132.5 ms limit) and nearly flaked on image-heavy (17.88 ms vs an 18.0 ms limit) on the very first real CI run. Each baselineMs below is set just above its observed CI mean; with the retained per-benchmark toleranceFraction the effective limits sit ≈2x the observed mean — a stable gate against a shared-runner's variance that still catches a genuine >2x throughput regression (the concurrency *correctness* proof is separately guaranteed by the raster-concurrency-stress pixel-identity lane, not this throughput gate). Still 'calibrated': false pending a multi-run statistical calibration.
pendingRecalibration: UPDATED (image-XObject rasterization fix): Documents.ImageXObjectResolver is now wired up, so RasterizeImageHeavyPage's six images actually decode and paint — the largest legitimate throughput shift this benchmark will ever see. That could not be re-measured on the linux-CI runner platform from this change alone (no push, no additional GitHub Actions spend), so RasterizeImageHeavyPage.baselineMs below is a DELIBERATELY PROVISIONAL interim bump, not a multi-run statistical CI calibration: measured via `--job short --filter '*RasterizeBenchmarks*'` (ci.yml's own exact invocation) on a mac-arm64 dev machine (text 31.245 ms, image 36.855 ms, transparency 8.348 ms), then scaled by the ~2.02x mac-to-linux-CI ratio this same file's own history already established for single-threaded work (text 62.85/31.245 = 2.012x, transparency 16.87/8.348 = 2.021x on the last real CI run) to extrapolate a linux-CI image estimate of ~74.3 ms, plus headroom. 'calibrated' stays false. .github/workflows/raster-perf-calibration.yml (unchanged) is still the real follow-up: run it once resources allow, then replace this extrapolated baselineMs with the actual multi-run linux-CI mean and flip 'calibrated' to true. JPEG 2000/JPXDecode: RasterizeJpxScanPage below was reseeded from a linux raster-perf-gate run (134.19 ms mean) once ci.yml's --buildTimeout 900 made that job measure again (it had been silently inert - every benchmark NA - since BenchmarkDotNet's default 2-minute boilerplate build timeout started expiring on the 2-vCPU runner). A single ShortRun measurement, so 'calibrated' stays false for it too until a multi-run calibration lands. The resampling-knob change (PLACEHOLDERS ADDED, STILL NOT SEEDED): RasterizeScanPageMinify and RasterizeScanPageMagnify (RasterizeBenchmarks.cs) exist in the benchmark suite and are already picked up by ci.yml's '*RasterizeBenchmarks*' filter; they previously carried NO 'benchmarks' entry below at all, so the perf gate skipped them silently (measured-vs-stored only compares keys the file names) even though CI was already spending runtime on them. Per the same-shape self-contained one-page-scan-benchmark lesson this file itself records two entries above (RasterizeJpxScanPage's own history) — such a baseline is SEEDED FROM THE LINUX CI RUNNER, never a mac extrapolation — so, exactly as with RasterizeJpxScanPage's own first-shipped value, the two entries below are an UNDISGUISED 300.0 ms placeholder (not computed via the file's own mac-to-linux-CI ratio method, deliberately) so the gate at least catches a catastrophic regression instead of checking nothing at all. A mac-arm64 dev-machine run (`--job short --filter '*RasterizeScanPage*'`, ShortRun IterationCount=3) measured RasterizeScanPageMinify 18.458 ms (StdDev 0.014 ms) and RasterizeScanPageMagnify 12.532 ms (StdDev 0.012 ms) — recorded here as evidence only, not as the baseline. The exact procedure remains the follow-up: after the next CI push, read the raster-perf-gate job's MEASURED lines for these two keys (never a WARN) and replace the 300.0 ms placeholders with a real linux-CI-observed baselineMs (toleranceFraction 0.35 like RasterizeJpxScanPage) on the following push — until then 'calibrated' stays false and these two keys are placeholders, not measurements.

RasterizeBenchmarks.RasterizeTextHeavyPa.description: 55 short paragraphs (~9pt) on one A4 page at 2048px width — glyph-shaping and glyph-rasterization throughput. Linux-CI observed mean 62.85 ms; limit 132 ms at the default 1.0 tolerance.

RasterizeBenchmarks.RasterizeImageHeavyP.description: Six distinct 300x200 gradient images stacked on one A4 page at 2048px width — image-XObject decode/blit throughput. PROVISIONAL: images now actually paint (Documents.ImageXObjectResolver wired), so the prior 19.0 ms baseline (measured with imageResolver: null, i.e. an image-free page) no longer reflects this benchmark's real work. Extrapolated from a mac-arm64 dev-machine measurement of 36.855 ms scaled by this file's own ~2.02x mac-to-linux-CI ratio (~74.3 ms) plus headroom, pending the real multi-run linux-CI calibration (see 'pendingRecalibration'); limit 164 ms at the default 1.0 tolerance.

RasterizeBenchmarks.RasterizeTransparenc.description: A rotated watermark plus four partially-transparent corner stamps over body content, one A4 page at 2048px width — alpha-compositing throughput. Linux-CI observed mean 16.87 ms; limit 36 ms at the default 1.0 tolerance.

RasterizeBenchmarks.RasterizeFourDocumen.description: Four independent PdfDocument.Open + Rasterize calls (each its own scratch ObjectRegistry) racing via Parallel.For — wall-clock throughput, wider tolerance than the single-page suites since a shared CI runner's core count and neighbour load vary far more than single-threaded throughput does (first two CI runs spanned ≤132 ms to 203 ms). Linux-CI observed mean 203.07 ms; limit 525 ms at the 1.5 tolerance.

RasterizeBenchmarks.RasterizeJpxScanPage.description: A self-contained one-page PDF (composed byte-wise in [GlobalSetup], no filesystem/corpus dependency) placing the same 640x480 JP2_SCAN_B64 literal generate_image_fixtures.py embeds for jpx-scan.pdf (9/7 irreversible, ICT, -r 20, tiled RPCL - a real-world W-9 scan shape) full-page - JPX decode-and-paint throughput. SEEDED FROM THE LINUX CI RUNNER, never a mac extrapolation: a raster-perf-gate run (ubuntu 24.04, AMD EPYC 9V45 2 vCPU, ShortRun IterationCount=3) measured mean 134.19 ms, StdDev 5.35 ms; baselineMs is set just above that observed mean, so with toleranceFraction 0.35 the limit is 189 ms - tight enough to catch a ~1.4x regression while leaving shared-runner headroom. History: the key first shipped as an undisguised 300 ms placeholder because raster-perf-gate had been silently INERT (BenchmarkDotNet's 2-minute boilerplate-build timeout expired on the 2-vCPU runner, every benchmark reported NA and the check only warned) - ci.yml now passes --buildTimeout 900 and this is the first measured run. A local mac-arm64 run of the same benchmark measured 148.7 ms (StdDev 8.9, N=3) - recorded as evidence only. 'calibrated' stays false until a multi-run calibration workflow runs.

RasterizeBenchmarks.RasterizeScanPageMin.description: A self-contained one-page scan-shaped placement rendered through the minify (Box-filter) regime — CI perf-gate coverage of the resampling knob's minify path. SEEDED from the linux-CI MEASURED line of a raster-perf-gate run (ubuntu-24.04, ci.yml raster-perf-gate, ShortRun N=3): mean 53.45 ms; baseline 55.0 ms with the RasterizeJpxScanPage tolerance 0.35 (limit 74.2 ms) — the same seeding procedure (a MEASURED line, never a WARN or a mac extrapolation). Inherits the gate's one-sided, pendingRecalibration debt.

RasterizeBenchmarks.RasterizeScanPageMag.description: The same scan-shaped placement rendered through the magnify (Bilinear/Nearest) regime — CI perf-gate coverage of the resampling knob's magnify path, a hot path that had NO regression guard at all before this entry existed. SEEDED from the linux-CI MEASURED line of a raster-perf-gate run (ubuntu-24.04, ci.yml raster-perf-gate, ShortRun N=3): mean 37.16 ms; baseline 40.0 ms with the RasterizeJpxScanPage tolerance 0.35 (limit 54.0 ms) — the same seeding procedure (a MEASURED line, never a WARN or a mac extrapolation). Inherits the gate's one-sided, pendingRecalibration debt.
